forecast_notes.nowcast: The production model does not yet estimate a separate time-evolution process. The nowcast therefore reports the current measured environment under the same uncertainty structure rather than inventing a distinct precision level.
forecast_notes.election_day: The official baseline is the election-outcome forecast under the current prospective model specification. Future political movement is represented through uncertainty, not an editorial trend adjustment.

methodology.partisan_lean: 5% 2016 + 20% 2020 + 75% 2024 district/state presidential margin, each centred on that year's national D−R margin
methodology.national_environment: 35-day generic-ballot poll average with exponential recency decay, sample-size and upstream source-quality weighting; partisan-sponsored polls downweighted
methodology.race_polling: nominee-matched polls from the last 55 days blended with the prior; weight rises sub-linearly with poll count and is capped
methodology.race_probability: normal-error conversion of expected two-party margin; uncertainty narrows only within the documented race-poll blend
methodology.probabilities: 30,000 correlated Monte Carlo chamber simulations with shared national and race-specific error
methodology.qualitative_news: not an input to numerical probabilities
methodology.senate_control: Democratic caucus requires 51 seats because the vice president is Republican

provenance.note: MIDTERM SIGNALS consumes factual/curated election inputs from the upstream repository, not its forecast probabilities. Numerical transformations and simulations are performed here.

limitations: No leakage-free 2018/2022 production replays are available yet; historical Brier/log-loss metrics are therefore withheld.
Candidate-quality effects beyond incumbency are not separately estimated.
Third-party and ranked-choice transfer behaviour is simplified in the chamber model.
Presidential-approval and economic-context feeds are not yet validated production inputs; FEC finance and external-forecaster data are displayed only in the separate non-model context layer.
The nowcast and election-day forecast do not yet use a separate explicit time-evolution process.
Correlated national error is simulated, but cross-race correlation remains deliberately simple rather than a full geographic covariance model.

briefing.thirty_second_read: MIDTERM SIGNALS gives Democrats a 95% probability of House control and a 71% probability of Senate control. The current weighted generic congressional ballot is D+8.4. The House 80% Democratic-seat interval is 222–257; the Senate interval is 49–54.
